input.body:
EMERGENCY WARRANTY CALLBACK: Ref TKT-F7420B (follows JOB-8802)
Request title: Boiler failure - no heating or hot water, pressure at zero
Address: Flat 3, 18 Maple Road, London SE15 4QJ (2nd floor, purpose-built block)
Tenant: Amara Okafor, +44 7700 900501
Request description: Vaillant ecoTEC (installed by you, 2019). Pressure gauge at zero, no heating or hot water since last night. This is the 3rd pressure-loss failure since August (JOB-8801 14 Aug, PRV replaced; JOB-8802 20 Sep, expansion vessel replaced, 90-day callback warranty). There is an infant in the household, so please attend TODAY.
Thank you for confirming by phone that you can attend. Please reply with:
1) your confirmed arrival window today,
2) written confirmation that this is covered under the JOB-8802 callback warranty (no charge),
3) after the visit, the root cause of the repeated pressure loss, what you did, photos, and your professional view on whether the boiler needs a replacement assessment.
Access: the tenant is usually home. Please call her 30 minutes before arrival. The concierge is on site Mon-Fri 8-6.
Please book the appointment as soon as possible with the tenant. If you have already scheduled an appointment, reply with the date and time. Note: your online booking system was returning errors (HTTP 504) today.

Hello, this is the managing agency. Please check your email about the EMERGENCY boiler warranty callback at Flat 3, 18 Maple Road, SE15 4QJ (ref TKT-F7420B). Please reply with your arrival time today.

Dear Amara,
I'm very sorry the boiler has failed again. We have logged this as an emergency (ref TKT-F7420B) because you have a young baby at home.
Thames Heating, the Gas Safe engineers who carried out the last repair, will attend today under the warranty from that repair, so there is no cost to you. They have not yet given us an exact arrival time. They will call you about 30 minutes before they arrive, and we will message you as soon as we have the time.
We have asked them to find out why the pressure keeps dropping, not just top it up again.
In the meantime:
- Please don't keep re-pressurising the boiler. If you see any water leaking from the boiler, pipes or radiators, put a towel or bowl under it and tell the engineer.
- Keep yourself and your baby as warm as you can, with extra layers and blankets and by staying in the warmest room.
- If you smell gas or a carbon monoxide alarm sounds, open the windows, don't use any electrical switches, leave the flat and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 straight away.
If you have any pets, please let the engineer know. If no one has contacted you by 2pm, please reply here and we will chase them.

Address: Flat 3, 18 Maple Road, London SE15 4QJ
Hi Priya,
I'm writing to let you know about an emergency repair today (ref TKT-F7420B). The tenant reported: "Hi, the boiler has stopped working again. No heating and no hot water since last night. The pressure gauge is on zero. This is the third time since August. I have a 4 month old baby here and the flat is freezing. Please can someone come today?"
As you have instructed, we have sent Thames Heating, and they have confirmed by phone that they will attend today. This is the third pressure-loss failure in about 8 weeks: PRV replaced on 14 Aug (£165) and expansion vessel replaced on 20 Sep (£240). The 20 Sep repair has a 90-day callback warranty, so we have asked Thames Heating to treat this visit as a warranty callback at no cost to you. We will tell you if they say otherwise before any charge is agreed.
Because this boiler (Vaillant ecoTEC, 2019) has now needed three repairs for the same fault in under 12 months, we recommend a replacement assessment. We have asked Thames Heating for their professional view after today's visit. Can you please let us know if you would like us to get a quote for a replacement, or a second quote for comparison?
We will update you once the engineer has attended.

Their booking system was down, so the job couldn't be booked properly, and I've passed the follow-up to the property manager (ESC-CAC52F, high priority). - **Urgency: emergency.** The boiler has failed with no heating or hot water, and there's a baby in the household.

**What I did**
1. **Ticket:** opened TKT-F7420B as an emergency.
2. **Thames Heating:** their availability system returned a timeout error twice, so there was no slot I could book. I phoned them instead (the call ran in simulated mode). They agreed to come today and to ring the tenant 30 minutes before. I followed up by email and SMS asking for an arrival time and written confirmation that the warranty covers this visit.
3. **Backup:** GasSure London (Gas Safe, £140 call-out, within the £500 emergency limit) has slots today at 13:00–15:00 and 16:00–18:00. I haven't booked them, to avoid paying for two contractors.
4. **Tenant (WhatsApp):** told her an engineer is coming today but the time isn't fixed yet, at no cost to her. I added safety and keep-warm advice, asked her to mention any pets, and asked her to reply if nobody has contacted her by 2pm.
5. **Landlord (email):** told her about the emergency and that we're claiming the warranty. I recommended a replacement assessment, since this is the third repair for the same fault within a year.
6. **Records:** added an internal note and set the case status.

**What the property manager needs to do today**
- Get a confirmed arrival time from Thames, then send the tenant the appointment confirmation.
- If there's no time by about 12:00, book GasSure for this afternoon and tell the landlord the same day.
- Push back if Thames tries to charge, as the 20 Sep warranty should cover this.
- After the visit, get the cause and photos, and take the landlord's decision on replacing the boiler.

**Things I noticed**
- **Contractor choice:** our policy says not to prefer a contractor whose repair has failed twice, and Thames's has. I used them anyway because the landlord asked for them and the visit is free under warranty. If this fix fails, GasSure should give a second opinion.
- **Dates don't match:** the case date is 21 Sep, the tenant's message is dated 9 Oct and the ticket system shows 10 Oct. The next steps are the same whichever is right.
- **Baby's age:** the tenancy record says there was a 4-month-old at check-in in June 2025, but the tenant says her baby is 4 months old now. The vulnerability note on the tenancy needs updating.
